facts.claim: "Darlin'" is track 1 on Cassandra Lewis's album Always, All Ways, released August 19, 2022 on Low Country Sound/Elektra.
Bandcamp lists "Darlin'" as a separate release dated May 2021, before the album came out.
Lewis wrote, composed and arranged all songs on the album, including "Darlin'".
The album was produced by David Jacobs-Strain and Christopher Worth with Cassandra Lewis, with additional production by Graham Patzner. Jacobs-Strain mixed it at Grange in Sisters, Oregon.

Basic tracks were recorded by Nino Moschella at Bird & Egg Studios in Richmond, CA. Additional tracks were recorded by Jacobs-Strain and Worth at The Rhududu in Portland, OR. Telegraph Audio in Portland mastered the album.

Credited players on "Darlin'" are Aviva LeFey (acoustic bass), Graham Patzner (piano), Scott Ferreter (bass guitar), Dan Schwartz (drums), JP Garau (Hammond organ), Trevor Bahnson (electric guitar), Greg Leisz (pedal steel) and Chris Hoog (saxophone).

According to her First Avenue bio, "Darlin'" reached half a million streams and built early buzz. Lewis then performed for Elektra Records President Gregg Nadel in the label's parking garage and ended up with a deal.
Lewis says the album's overarching theme is her relationship with a man she compares to The Wizard of Oz.

Lewis began writing the album while working on cannabis farms in Mendocino County. She funded the recording through shows and loans, and she says the live band tracks were cut at Bird & Egg Studios in Richmond, CA.
Lewis calls her sound "Cosmic Americana". The album peaked at #1 on the KEXP (Seattle) Americana radio chart. Her next project was set to be a Dave Cobb-produced Low Country Sound/Elektra release.

research.lineage: Cassandra Lewis, a Nashville-based singer-songwriter, describes her music as "Cosmic Americana", rooted in classic country, blues, soul and psychedelic rock.

draft:
A walking bass line isn't what you expect under a fingerpicked acoustic guitar. On **Darlin'**, the guitar rolls out its arpeggios like a folk song, patient and close. Underneath, the bass moves step by step the way it would in an old soul ballad or a honky-tonk slow dance. That pairing is what Cassandra Lewis means by "Cosmic Americana," her name for music rooted in classic country, blues, soul and psychedelic rock. Here the country and the soul share one floor, and neither is asked to leave.

The tempo is slow and the groove sways. The drums keep it plain: kick, snare, hi-hat, nothing showy. Over that, Lewis sings in a clear voice with a slight vibrato, holding her notes instead of clipping them. There are no harmonies. Nobody doubles her or answers her, and that shapes how the song feels. A song called "Darlin'" is an address, words aimed at one person, and the arrangement respects that by leaving the voice alone in the room. You can hear the room itself, a natural reverb and a clean, polished finish. The band seems to stand a few feet back to give the singer space.

What a listener carries away is tenderness with some weight to it. Sustained notes ask you to wait. A walking bass keeps time like someone who isn't going anywhere. Lewis has said the album this song opens is about her relationship with a man she compares to The Wizard of Oz. The song doesn't need to spell that story out to hold its mood. The steady playing and the exposed, unharmonized voice sit side by side, warmth and openness at once, and neither cancels the other.

The backstory adds to its pull. Lewis started writing the record while working on cannabis farms in Mendocino County, and she paid for the sessions with shows and loans. She wrote and arranged every song herself. "Darlin'" came out on its own in 2021, more than a year before the album. It reached half a million streams and built enough buzz that she ended up singing for Elektra president Gregg Nadel in the label's parking garage and leaving with a deal. It's fitting that it leads off *Always, All Ways*: the song that opened the door also opens the record.

The live band tracks were cut at Bird & Egg in Richmond, California, with Scott Ferreter on bass guitar and Dan Schwartz on drums. The credits also list Greg Leisz on pedal steel, JP Garau on Hammond organ, Graham Patzner on piano and Chris Hoog on saxophone.

"Darlin'" makes you feel what it's like to be spoken to slowly and on purpose, by someone who has chosen to stay in the room.
